name: visual-qa
title: Visual & Responsive QA
summary: Automated visual, responsive and quality QA with a real browser: drive the app with Playwright across a device matrix, catch horizontal overflow / clipped elements / broken layout, verify contrast + WCAG a11y, measure CLS/LCP, gate Lighthouse >= 95, and pixel-diff against baselines (BackstopJS). Ships the closed loop — start app -> screenshot matrix -> detect -> hand fixes to the developer -> re-verify -> before/after report. Feeds the visual-qa, responsive, frontend and mobile agents.
mandatory_tests: The app is driven in a real browser (Playwright) across the full device matrix — not just one viewport
No horizontal overflow (document scrollWidth <= viewport width) on any tested viewport
No clipped/off-screen interactive elements; nav, buttons and CTAs are fully visible and reachable
Lighthouse category scores >= 95 (Performance, Accessibility, Best-Practices, SEO) on the key routes
Cumulative Layout Shift < 0.1 and no unsized media causing shift
validations: Every key route is verified across the device matrix (360x640, 390x844, 768x1024, 1024x768, 1366x768, 1920x1080) plus named devices (iPhone SE/15/16, Pixel 9, Galaxy S24, iPad)
Color contrast meets WCAG 2.2 AA in light AND dark; focus is visible; targets >= 24px (44px on touch)
Visual regressions are caught by pixel diff against approved baselines (BackstopJS) — intentional changes re-approved, never blindly overwritten
Findings are reported with before/after screenshots; the fix is applied by the owning developer (responsive/frontend/mobile) and re-verified green
Thresholds run in CI (Playwright + Lighthouse CI) so a regression blocks the merge, not just local runs
